subject: Embeddings endpoint latency spike after catalog update - urgent
messages:
From: Maya R. <support@acme.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+eng@acme.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: sudden slowdown on embeddings after update

Hi Dev,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency for your embeddings endpoint (model: open-embed-3-small, catalog tag v2.3.1) right after the catalog push this morning. Our automated checks show p95 jumped from ~140ms to ~1.9s and p99 to ~4.2s on live traffic. This is impacting our search relevance and downstream pipelines.

Attached are a handful of sampled queries and timing traces. Can you confirm if the model promotion triggered anything on your side? This is high priority for us — currently 18% of inference calls are hitting >2s.

Thanks,
Maya
Acme AI — Platform Reliability
attachments: acme_latency_samples_dec06.csv, traces_acme_120627.pcap
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maya R. <support@acme.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden slowdown on embeddings after update

Hi Maya — thanks for the quick flag.

We rolled catalog tag v2.3.1 at 08:45 PST to promote open-embed-3-small with updated kernel candidates and a quantization profile. Early canaries looked fine, but we see the same p95/p99 bump in our internal dashboards now.

A few immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether the affected traffic is hitting our hosted endpoint or a dedicated pool?
- If you can share a short example query and the timestamp we can map to traces.

I'm looping in Neha (SRE) and Laura (Customer Success) — we'll mobilize and get back with a plan in 20–30 min.

— Dev
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Maya R. <support@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden slowdown on embeddings after update

Thanks Maya — I pulled Acme's traffic and traces. Quick summary:
- Catalog push at 08:45 included a new kernel selection path that prefers an optimized kernel set for long-context workloads.
- KV-cache invalidation policy was toggled (LRU->aggressive TTL reset) as part of the rollout; this appears to increase cold-starts for many batched requests.
- We see GPU memory churn on some hosts which coincides with higher tail latency.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
1) Pin Acme's customer routing to the previous catalog tag (v2.3.0) for their API key — performing now.
2) Rolling a targeted rollback of the aggressive KV TTL change for shared pools.
3) Enabling finer-grained tracing for a subset (10%) of their requests to capture KV cache hits/misses and kernel selection logs.

I'll confirm after the pin completes (~10 min). If pinning reduces p99, we'll keep Acme on v2.3.0 until we have a fix.

-Neha (SRE)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maya R. <support@acme.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden slowdown on embeddings after update

On Mon, 06 Dec 2027 at 09:42, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Maya — I pulled Acme's traffic and traces. Quick summary:
> - Catalog push at 08:45 included a new kernel selection path that prefers an optimized kernel set for long-context workloads.
> - KV-cache invalidation policy was toggled (LRU->aggressive TTL reset) as part of the rollout; this appears to increase cold-starts for many batched requests.

Maya — confirming Neha's note: we've pinned Acme's API key back to v2.3.0 at 09:58 PST and are seeing an immediate reduction in tail latency on the pinned sessions. Preliminary numbers: p95 down from 1.9s -> 180ms; p99 down from 4.2s -> 550ms. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps (internal + customer):
- Neha to finish the targeted rollback for the global pool change and run load checks.
- Rishi and Tessa to investigate kernel selection heuristics that caused suboptimal paths for Acme's typical request lengths.
- Laura to coordinate a short postmortem and customer-facing note.

Laura — can you propose what we tell Acme about credits/SLAs if their production queries were impacted for ~90 minutes?

— Dev
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Maya R. <support@acme.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Customer update + proposed credits

Hi Maya — thanks again for raising this and for the traces. Apologies for the disruption. Short customer update we can send now:

1) Root cause (high-level): A catalog promotion included a kernel-selection path and a KV-cache TTL change that together increased tail latency for some production patterns.
2) Immediate action taken: We pinned Acme traffic to the previous catalog version (v2.3.0) at 09:58 PST which reduced p95/p99 substantially. The global KV TTL change has been rolled back for shared pools.
3) Next steps: We will run a controlled replay of your sampled queries against the v2.3.1 artifacts with additional runtime flags (metrics tracing enabled) and publish a technical postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

Compensation proposal:
- A one-time credit equal to 5% of the last monthly invoice or the equivalent of two days of quota at peak usage (whichever is larger).
- Priority rollout for a hotfix and a follow-up review with engineering within 48 hours.

If that sounds reasonable I will send a formal note and CC billing.

— Laura
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maya R. <support@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 18:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Follow-up: short summary + exec note

Maya — quick executive summary for your leadership and ours:
- Incident window: 08:45–09:58 PST on 2027-12-06.
- Impact: p95 increased from ~140ms to ~1.9s; p99 increased to ~4.2s for affected traffic. Estimated affected call volume: 18% of their traffic during the window.
- Cause: combination of new kernel-selection heuristics and an aggressive KV-cache invalidation change in catalog v2.3.1.
- Mitigation: pinned Acme to v2.3.0, rolled back global KV TTL change, monitoring shows restoration of normal tail-latency.
- Compensation: Laura proposed a one-time credit (5% monthly invoice).
- Engineering action items (owners):
  * Kernel heuristics review & deterministic tests (Rishi, Tessa) — 48h.
  * Hardening canary and automatic rollback playbook for catalog pushes (Neha) — 72h.
  * Customer replay and technical postmortem (Dev + Rishi) — EOD next day.

We will send a formal note and a postmortem link (HubSpot:HS-22014) once the replay completes. Please let us know if you'd like a briefing call this afternoon (we can do 3:30–4:30 PST).

Thanks again for patience — we're treating this as an urgent escalation.

— Dev
